verdict.rationale: Granola's docs give some first-party detail on how transcription works. They state that it captures computer audio rather than sending a bot, that it supports 31 transcription languages on desktop and 17 on mobile, and that it labels speakers as Me/Them by default with optional speaker tags. The docs never name the transcription models and make no accuracy or quality claims. missing for 10: named transcription models/providers, accuracy or WER claims, documented known limits (accents, noise, crosstalk, per-language quality), independent accuracy corroboration.

support.subject: As a product manager, the vendor documents how transcription actually works and its quality (models, accuracy claims, known limits) rather than just saying "AI-powered"

citations.quote: Uses your computer audio, so doesn't invite a bot
Granola supports 31 languages on desktop (macOS and Windows) and 17 languages on mobile (iOS and Android).
Speaker tags show each participant's name above their parts of the conversation, giving you more detailed attribution than the default Me and Them labels.
